title: Add Bluetooth file receiving to the Bluetooth panel
head: e90879d25dc1
workflow: Opus full review, Sol boundary hunter, Opus self-check of the draft, editorial check, batch gates

leads.summary: Default obexd also serves Bluetooth File Transfer on the Downloads root, bypassing Agent1 for FTP writes, reads, deletes and rename
leads.consequence: When a peer passes BlueZ's separate FTP service authorization (in particular a trusted paired peer), FTP PUT opens files with O_TRUNC, FTP DELETE removes files, FTP GET reads them, and FTP SETPATH may create directories, without calling AuthorizePush or claim_path. Thus the user-facing OPP-only/never-overwrite claims are not true for the service as started. The FTP profile is not automatically unauthenticated: BlueZ has authorize=true and prompts an agent unless the peer is Trusted. Exclude the FTP plugin (for example obexd --noplugin ftp) while retaining the bluetooth transport and filesystem plugins if FTP is not intended.
leads.triage: corroborates Opus N1; coordinator verified ftp.c/obex.c/profile.c/adapter.c/agent-helper.c; published

leads.summary: Pairing is checked by remote address across every adapter, not by the adapter receiving the push
leads.consequence: On a two-controller machine where address AA:... is Paired on hci1 but not hci0, an incoming OPP session on hci0 from that address is accepted as paired; BlueZ's OPP profile uses low security without service authorization. Compare Session1.Source to Adapter1.Address and restrict the Device1 record to that adapter before accepting. This is conditional on the sender reaching the unpaired controller and is not evidence that a wholly unknown address passes.
leads.triage: behavioural edge, on-air reachability untested, low value; dropped

leads.summary: An accepted filename remains as an empty reserved file if obexd cannot open it
leads.consequence: Agent creates an O_EXCL placeholder before responding to AuthorizePush but never removes it. If obexd's subsequent open fails, the transfer never sets os->path and BlueZ's abort cleanup cannot remove it. Subsequent pushes of the same name skip that empty file and consume numbered variants; the user sees an empty download even though transfer failed. This is distinct from normal aborted transfers after a successful open, for which BlueZ does attempt removal.
leads.triage: overlaps Opus F2 minor note; cosmetic; not published

leads.summary: A valid escaped XDG Downloads path is parsed literally, sending files to a different folder
leads.consequence: xdg-user-dirs-update shell-escapes $, backslash and quotes, and xdg_user_dir_lookup unescapes them. For XDG_DOWNLOAD_DIR="$HOME/Reports\$2026", the agent resolves Reports\$2026 instead of the browser's Reports$2026, creates that new directory and starts obexd there. Use xdg-user-dir DOWNLOAD (or implement its exact unescaping/validation) rather than a greedy regex and simple replacement. The panel label is separately hardcoded.

leads.summary: Duplicate valid 255-byte filenames cannot be renamed even when other names are free
leads.consequence: The first 255-byte basename is claimed; the second attempt appends ' (1)' beyond NAME_MAX. os.open raises ENAMETOOLONG, claim_path returns None without trying a shortened variant, so a paired user's second push is refused instead of receiving a collision-free name. Byte-counted multibyte names near the same limit have the same problem.
leads.triage: reject is fail-safe; Opus S7 similar; not published

leads.summary: An already-running or D-Bus-activated stock obexd makes the opted-in receiver repeatedly fail
leads.consequence: bluez-obex ships a D-Bus-activatable obex.service. If it owns org.bluez.obex when the helper starts, main returns 1 rather than using, stopping, or coordinating with it; Restart=on-failure retries every two seconds, and the panel's is-on check paints OFF though the unit is enabled. After stopping the competing daemon, user may have to reset a start-rate limit or restart the unit if already failed. Separate server ownership/activation handling from the user-facing enable operation.
leads.triage: overlaps Opus N4 and S11 startup refusal; low; not published

leads.summary: The new tests do not catch an auto-accept launch that bypasses their policy tests
leads.consequence: A plausible one-flag regression adding --auto-accept to subprocess.Popen([OBEXD, '--nodetach', '--root', directory]) leaves the file's checks green: the grep only checks the unit for bt-obex; Python tests construct Receiver with fakes and never execute main, RegisterAgent or obexd. BlueZ's opp_chkput then skips AuthorizePush entirely, accepting even unpaired pushes and overwriting names. Add a test asserting the spawned obexd command excludes auto-accept (and a private-bus integration test for the policy) so this mutant fails.
leads.triage: unrun lead; covered by Opus run-verified surviving mutants M05/M12; folded into Optional test improvement

leads.summary: Open PR #11260 overlaps the new files section and connection-action timer in Bluetooth Panel.qml
leads.consequence: The two unstacked heads both edit visibleSections and insert timer/process blocks at the same place. A three-way git merge-file using #11260's own merge-base produces conflicts; choosing its visibleSections arm drops the new file row from j/k, and choosing only this PR's timer arm drops #11260's connection completion UI. Preserve ['files'].concat(Model.visibleSections(deviceGroups, showDiscoveredDevices)) and both process/timer groups while resolving. GitHub currently labels #11260 MERGEABLE against its base, not against this PR.
leads.triage: routine textual churn, overlaps Opus Q6; not published

leads.summary: Open PRs #12585 and #12897 collide with receiver fixtures in bluetooth-test.sh
leads.consequence: Both heads are unstacked with this PR. A three-way merge of each PR's own test using that PR's merge-base yields conflict markers: #12585's rfkill blocked-state assertions and this PR's appended receiver helper fixture occupy the same end-of-file insertion, while #12897's new pairing-agent checks overlap this PR's initial agent tests. Resolving by selecting either side drops a whole feature's regression coverage; retain both blocks. Their panel QML merges without markers but this test file does not.

leads.summary: Panel reports a fixed ~/DOWNLOADS even when receiver stores in configured XDG directory
leads.consequence: With a valid XDG_DOWNLOAD_DIR=$HOME/Telechargements (the new test explicitly exercises that value), the active switch still displays PUSH → ~/DOWNLOADS. Users looking there will not find received files. Show the effective directory from the helper or use a generic 'RECEIVING' label if the path is not available to the panel.
leads.triage: corroborates Opus N2; cosmetic; not published

limits: No HCI, btvirt, real obexd or live Bluetooth link was run; H1 and H2 are demonstrated by pinned BlueZ source and local argument fixtures, not an on-air exploit. FTP service authorization must not be described as unrestricted: BlueZ marks FTP authorize=true.
Full merged runtime tests for overlapping open PRs were not run; H8 is a demonstrated merge-file conflict plus code-shape consequence, not an upstream merge-state claim.

## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

Follow-up at `e90879d2` to the [earlier review](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/12766#issuecomment-5791584885) and the [author's reply](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/12766#issuecomment-5844199226). Both earlier findings are resolved for the Object Push path. One new issue: the obexd the agent starts also serves OBEX File Transfer on the downloads directory, and that path bypasses the agent.

| Earlier finding | At `e90879d2` |
|---|---|
| Paired-only restriction not enforced | **Resolved** for Object Push |
| Duplicate filename can overwrite a download | **Resolved** for Object Push |

**Verified:** obexd's Object Push handler calls the agent's `AuthorizePush` for every push, and the agent rejects senders that BlueZ does not list as `Paired`. It also rejects sessions whose root is not the agent's directory and fails closed when BlueZ cannot be read; with no agent registered, obexd rejects the push itself. The agent claims the destination with `O_EXCL`, and obexd opens exactly that path, with no rename. In an isolated D-Bus harness against a stand-in obexd, unpaired and unknown pushes, and a push while BlueZ was unreachable, created no file, and the agent refused to start next to an obexd it had not started. A second `report.pdf` landed as `report (1).pdf`, and the first file stayed byte-identical. `bluetooth-test.sh` passes at this head (83 assertions, including a foreign-root rejection), and the updated test fails against the earlier head `43aff5ce`.

**Paired versus Trusted (author's note):** the note is accurate. With Omarchy's `bt-agent` accepting pairings, `Paired` is only as strong as whoever can bond, and `Trusted` would limit acceptance to devices the user paired or connected from the panel (Omarchy's pair and connect actions mark the device trusted), which excludes devices that bonded on their own through `bt-agent`. That is a maintainer choice. It does not change the File Transfer issue below, because that path does not go through this agent.

## The receiver also exposes OBEX File Transfer on the downloads directory

The agent starts `/usr/lib/bluetooth/obexd --nodetach --root <downloads>` with no plugin restriction ([agent](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/blob/e90879d25dc152b070396581a8f67e09a59bafc1/bin/omarchy-bluetooth-files-agent#L358)). obexd then loads all of its built-in services, and File Transfer (also reused by PC Suite) works directly on that root. Only Object Push asks the agent ([`opp.c`](https://github.com/bluez/bluez/blob/5.87/obexd/plugins/opp.c#L63-L69)). The File Transfer write path, [`ftp_chkput`](https://github.com/bluez/bluez/blob/5.87/obexd/plugins/ftp.c#L156-L189), goes straight to [`obex_put_stream_start`](https://github.com/bluez/bluez/blob/5.87/obexd/src/obex.c#L706-L721), which opens the target with `O_WRONLY|O_CREAT|O_TRUNC`. File Transfer also supports listing, reading and deleting files in the root.

```text
Source-derived, not reproduced over a real radio:
Object Push   -> agent AuthorizePush (Paired check, O_EXCL claim) -> new file
File Transfer -> bluetoothd service authorization (Trusted: allowed; else bt-agent: any Paired)
              -> O_TRUNC open, no agent call -> existing download overwritten
```

File Transfer is registered with `authorize = true` ([`profile.c`](https://github.com/bluez/bluez/blob/5.87/src/profile.c#L2163-L2172)), bluetoothd admits trusted devices without asking an agent ([`adapter.c`](https://github.com/bluez/bluez/blob/5.87/src/adapter.c#L7783-L7786)), and Omarchy's `bt-agent` approves service authorization for any other paired device ([bluez-tools `agent-helper.c`](https://github.com/khvzak/bluez-tools/blob/7cb788c9c43facfd2d14ff50e16d6a19f033a6a7/src/lib/agent-helper.c#L67-L69)). So pairing still gates this path, but switching the agent's check to `Trusted` would not change it.

**Impact:** while the receiver is on, a paired peer that uses File Transfer (another computer, or a misbehaving paired device) can overwrite, read or delete files in the downloads directory. That contradicts the stated guarantee that "a push can never land on an existing download" and goes beyond "accept files". Android's share sheet uses Object Push, so the ordinary phone flow is unaffected.

**Suggested change:** start obexd with only the plugins Object Push needs, for example `--plugin opp,filesystem,bluetooth` (obexd accepts a comma-separated list), and add a test that pins the spawned command line.

**Packaging note:** the unit file ships only through the companion omarchy-pkgs#576. Without it, `config-test.sh` fails ("PKGBUILD does not explicitly install …omarchy-bluetooth-files.service"), and package installs get the helper and agent without the unit.

**Optional test improvement:** the new tests call `Receiver.authorize` against fakes, so some agent regressions still pass all 83 assertions. For example, a mutant that accepts pushes when the BlueZ query fails, or one that starts obexd without `--root`. One test that checks the spawned obexd argv and the BlueZ-error branch would catch these.

---

## Review information

**Test scope:** source inspection of this head, the earlier head `43aff5ce`, BlueZ 5.87 and Arch's pinned bluez-tools. Repository tests and an isolated D-Bus harness with a stand-in obexd and bluetoothd were run in a sandbox. No real Bluetooth transfers, File Transfer sessions or UI validation.

**AI process:** Opus 5.5 Medium coordination and synthesis, Opus 5.5 Xhigh technical review (its final report write-up ran on Opus 4.8 after an automatic model fallback) and final fact check, GPT 6 Sol Xhigh search for related issues, Opus 5.5 Medium editorial check.
